note.explanation: Acceleration tells us how quickly velocity changes. A change in velocity may be a change in speed, direction, or both.
examples: A car speeds up from rest: its velocity increases, so it has positive acceleration.
A moving car brakes and slows down: its velocity decreases, so it has negative acceleration.
note.checkAnswer: Acceleration is the change in velocity divided by the time taken: a_av = (v_f − v_i)/t.
note.simple: Acceleration is how quickly velocity changes. If velocity gets smaller, acceleration is negative.
note.checkQuestion: A body changes velocity from 4 m s⁻¹ to 10 m s⁻¹ in 3 s. What is its average acceleration?
note.title: Acceleration
steps: Find the change in velocity: v_f − v_i.
Divide the change in velocity by the time taken: a_av = (v_f − v_i)/t.
Write the answer in m s⁻².

mcqs.stem: A cyclist's velocity changes from 3 m s⁻¹ to 15 m s⁻¹ in 6 s. What is the average acceleration?
rationales: Correct: (15 − 3)/6 = 2 m s⁻².
This is the velocity change divided by 3 s, not 6 s.
This does not equal the velocity change divided by the time.
This is the velocity change without dividing by the time.

mcqs.stem: What is the SI unit of acceleration?
rationales: This is the SI unit of velocity, not acceleration.
Correct: acceleration is change in velocity per time, so its unit is m s⁻².

mcqs.stem: What is acceleration called when the time rate of change of velocity is constant?

rationales: This gives the magnitude but misses the negative sign for decreasing velocity.
Correct: (6 − 18)/4 = −3 m s⁻².

examTips: The board may ask you to define acceleration or distinguish positive acceleration, negative acceleration, and deceleration.
In numerical questions, write the given values first and convert km h⁻¹ to m s⁻¹ before using an equation.
For average acceleration, use a_av = (v_f − v_i)/t and include m s⁻² in the answer.
For constant acceleration, v_f = v_i + at is useful when the question asks for final velocity, initial velocity, acceleration, or time.
A negative answer for acceleration is important when velocity decreases; do not remove its minus sign.

explain.title: What acceleration means
explain.body: Acceleration is defined as the time rate of change of velocity. In other words, it tells how quickly velocity changes.

explain.title: Positive and negative acceleration
explain.body: The acceleration is positive if the velocity is increasing and it is negative if the velocity is decreasing. Negative acceleration is also called deceleration or retardation.

explain.title: Acceleration has direction
explain.body: Acceleration is a vector quantity like velocity, but the direction of acceleration is that of change of velocity. A change in velocity can occur in magnitude, direction, or both.

explain.title: Average acceleration
explain.body: If a body is moving with an initial velocity v_i and after some time t its velocity changes to v_f, the change in velocity is Δv = v_f − v_i that occurs in time t. In this case, rate of change of velocity i.e., acceleration will be average acceleration. Use a_av = (v_f − v_i)/t, and write the SI unit as m s⁻².

explain.title: Uniform and non-uniform acceleration
explain.body: If time rate of change of velocity is constant, the acceleration is said to be uniform. If anyone of the magnitude or direction or both of them changes it is called variable or non-uniform acceleration.

mistakes: Using km h⁻¹ directly in an equation when the other values are in SI units; convert it to m s⁻¹ first.
Reversing the subtraction in v_f − v_i, which can give the wrong sign.
Leaving out the minus sign when a body is slowing down.
Writing m s⁻¹ instead of the acceleration unit m s⁻².
Using v_f = v_i + at without checking that acceleration is constant.
